newsitem.title: India: Indian gold prices slump at close on fresh selling.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold prices slump at close on fresh selling.

text.p: ** Indian gold 24 carat closes 30 rupees lower at 4,630 rupees per 10 grammes against the previous close of 4,660 rupees
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) down 350 rupees at 54,200 rupees after losing 50 rupees on Thursday.
** Silver (.999) falls by 80 rupees at 6,715 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,795 rupees as losses in the world market triggers unloading by local stockists
Indian 24 carat gold prices on Friday ended 30 rupees lower at 4,630 rupees per 10 grammes on the back of a weak world market which prompted fresh selling locally, dealers said.
"Sluggish physical enquiries as well as a drop in the premiums of special licence to import gold also subdued market sentiment," said Babubhai Jain, a leading dealer.
"The licence premium slid to 10.70/10.80 percent from 11.25/11.50 percent," he added.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) closed 350 rupees lower at 54,200 rupees after losing 50 rupees on Thursday.
Silver (.999) fell by 80 rupees at 6,715 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,795 rupees amid losses in the world market.
